title: Lesson 16: Mentorship and Developing Senior Delivery Talent
description: How a practice develops the senior talent that stops it being capped by the principal, the four relationships hidden under the word mentorship, and the loop that actually transfers judgment instead of describing it.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Mentorship and Developing Senior Delivery Talent”, a high-potential operator two years from principal is already performing well. Which relationship do they actually need?
options: Mentorship on judgment and sponsorship into the room where the client relationship and the P and L live, because delivering more management is how a firm loses its best people.
More management, because objectives, utilization, and role performance are still unproven.
Coaching on how to work faster within the current role before any new exposure.
All four relationships at once so nothing is missed.
questions.explanation: The lesson says the advanced discipline is triage, and management answers whether someone is doing the job while sponsorship creates the opportunity mentorship turns into capability.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Mentorship and Developing Senior Delivery Talent”, the lesson says a conversation where the principal explains how they would have handled a situation does not transfer judgment. What does?
options: Handing the operator the written standard and letting them read it until it is memorized.
Letting the operator shadow the principal for a full year before making any decision.
Reviewing the operator's output against the acceptance criteria after each delivery.
A progression of observation, then simulated decisions where the operator commits before the principal reveals their answer, then earned autonomy with a backstop, then judgment with no backstop.
questions.explanation: The lesson says the delta between the operator's committed judgment and the principal's is the actual pedagogical content, and the discipline is to answer with the question rather than the answer.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Mentorship and Developing Senior Delivery Talent”, what distinguishes senior delivery talent from a mid-level operator?
options: More years of experience across a wider range of clients.
A higher utilization rate on client-billable work.
The ability to author the standard rather than only meet it: write the acceptance criteria, place the gate, review someone else's work, and own the estimate and the client relationship.
The habit of escalating fewer problems to the principal over time.
questions.explanation: The lesson says the step up is the move from executing within a framework to owning it, and that nobody becomes ready by being told they are not ready.
